policies.rule: Primary track-grant authority must order revocation with editorial commit; same MongoDB transaction is preferred.
Admin role does not imply global editorial scope; global scope is explicit and audited.
Authorized grantors manage grants; track delegates cannot exceed their own explicit scope.
A revocation committed before editorial commit denies that edit; an earlier confirmed edit remains historically valid.
Relevant user, role, and session changes require proven ordering; initial authentication is insufficient.
Static Python permission-matrix changes require coordinated policy version and writer transition.
Editorial changes and relevant authority changes require consistent audit.
No writer that can mutate protected state may bypass enforcement during cutover.

decisions.criterion: Approve one primary source, lifecycle, ownership, references, recovery, and audit.
Approve explicit independent provision/revoke and recovery; no implicit admin wildcard.
Name grantors, delegates, revokers, reviewers, emergency roles, and anti-escalation.

decisions.owner: Project owner; IAM and operations for mechanism
decisions.criterion: For each mutable authority state, show commit ordering in target or coordinated drain.
Approve hybrid epoch plus drain only after all writers and release transitions are covered.
Retest on approved baseline; capability stays server-issued and separate from fence/revision.
Approve versioning, preconditions, idempotency, null/absence, replay and conflict mapping.

Close ADR-008 through its separately authorized evidence process.
Approve preservation of sessions, generations, progress and attempts plus withdrawal semantics.
Rehearse rollback on approved target and obtain new exact implementation authorization.

enforcement_principles.single_editorial_revision_authority: C8/C10 by track; do not create a second revision authority
allow_requires: active explicit grant or explicit global scope
enforcement_principles.ambiguous_commit: reconcile by stable internal operation identity; never blindly repeat business mutation
enforcement_principles.external_replay: reauthorize currently and return minimum receipt only
enforcement_principles.privacy: no tokens, payloads, private response bodies or secrets in receipt/log/fingerprint

writers.enforcement: Track-scoped CAS/fence, trusted actor, idempotent reorder, atomic audit.

Authorize source and destination; staged, atomic-visible, idempotent compound intent.
Block until source-revision snapshot, immutable generation and atomic public-head swap plus reader coverage.
Resolve ancestry/track server-side; one track revision, CAS/fence and atomic audit.
Block deletes pending learner-state policy; stage/idempotently authorize compound clone.
Track CAS/fence plus audit/idempotency; cannot cut over before W-02/03/04/06/10/11/12/13 containment.
Transactional relation validation and mutation under W-05 track authority.
Investigate global catalog authority/epoch and cross-track snapshot effects.
Block until all writes share authority or import is globally coordinated, staged and recoverable.
Block until restore state machine is fenced per write and serialized with CRUD/import/publish.
Bind snapshot to exact source revision; serialize reconciliation and audit recovery.
Restrict to allowlisted disposable targets and keep seed identity outside cutover scope.
Classify migrations individually; approved preflight, compatibility and recovery; no hidden bypass.
Keep inactive; resolve external callers, ACL and source consistency before reuse.
Future session-aware audit contract must join required mutation transaction and minimize fields.
Outside operational scope only while isolated namespace/call graph remains unconsumed.

Order grant/user/session/policy state with editorial CAS/fence.

Only then propose a bounded writer family with persistent/concurrency tests.
Add publication/snapshot/readers, import/restore, deletions and learner state by dependency.
Rehearse rollback, obtain exact implementation and separate deployment authorization.
